help.title: Cox, Firth Bias Correction
help.body:
Cox Proportional Hazards Model with Firth Bias Correction

Fits a Cox proportional hazards model for time-to-event data with censored observations using Firth's penalized maximum likelihood bias reduction method. This has been shown to provide a solution in case of monotone likelihood (nonconvergence of the likelihood function). The phenomenon of monotone likelihood in a sample causes parameter estimates of a Cox model to diverge, with infinite standard errors. Therefore, classical maximum likelihood analysis fails; the usual Wald confidence intervals cover the whole range of real numbers. Monotone likelihood appears if there is single covariate or a linear combination of covariates such that at each event time, out of all individuals being at risk at that time, the individual with the highest (or at each event time the individual with the lowest) value for that covariate or linear combination experiences the event. It was shown that analysis by Firth's penalized likelihood method, particularly in conjunction with the computation of profile likelihood confidence intervals and penalized likelihood ratio tests is superior to maximum likelihood analysis. This model is also used in situations of small sample sizes and rare events where standard maximum likelihood is prone to bias.

Model fitting statistics, parameter estimates, and hazard ratios are provided. Options available include model diagnostics such as proportional hazards and covariate functional form assessments.

The dataset used to fit the model must have complete data for all variables involved. To remove missing values see Variables -> Missing Values -> Remove NAs.

Time: Time to event for those experiencing the event or time to last follow-up for those not experiencing the event

Event: Numerical event indicator; 1=event, 0=censor

Model expression builder for independent variables: Specify the function of the predictors that will be used to model the outcome risk. Factors, strings, and logical variables will be dummy coded.

Options

Type of test statistics and confidence intervals:
Specifies if confidence intervals and tests should be based on the profile penalized log likelihood (the default) or on the Wald method

Maximum number of iterations:
Specify the maximum number of iterations for the fitting routine. In cases of initial non-convergence, try increasing this to obtain convergence.

Maximum change of (standardized) parameter values allowed in one iteration (>0):
In cases of initial non-convergence, try decreasing this to obtain convergence, e.g. 0.1.

Model Diagnostics:
If selected, proportional hazards tests and plots will be provided, in addition to assessments of functional form for each covariate in the model. The null model Martingale residual axis minimum value option might need to be changed so that all residuals appear in the plot. To get functional form assessments, you must specify only numeric predictors.

References:

Firth D (1993). Bias reduction of maximum likelihood estimates. Biometrika 80:27--38.

Heinze G and Schemper M (2001). A Solution to the Problem of Monotone Likelihood in Cox Regression. Biometrics 57(1):114--119.

Heinze G (1999). Technical Report 10/1999: The application of Firth's procedure to Cox and logistic regression. Section of Clinical Biometrics, Department of Medical Computer Sciences, University of Vienna, Vienna.

Required R packages: coxphf, survival, survminer, dplyr
